title: Signed product fibers and normalized augmented Roos limits
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the module universe, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Assume countable products in $\mathcal A$ are exact, and use unbounded derived categories for $\mathcal A$ and its strict towers $\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A)=\operatorname{Fun}(\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category, lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian]. For a strict tower complex $X$, put $B_X=\prod_nX_n$ and $f_X=1-s_X$, where $\operatorname{pr}_ns_X=t_n\operatorname{pr}_{n+1}$. Define $\Phi(X)^i=B_X^i\oplus B_X^{i-1}$ and $d_\Phi(x,y)=(dx,f_Xx-dy)$, acting diagonally on strict tower morphisms. Let $\mathsf C(X)=\operatorname{Cone}(f_X)[-1]$ have differential $d(y,x)=(-dy-f_Xx,dx)$ [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Write $Q$ for derived localization, and let $\rho_X:Q\mathsf C(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim X$ be the comparison normalized on a K-injective tower resolution $q:X\to I$ by the inverse of the ordinary-limit inclusion $\lim I\to\mathsf C(I)$, $z\mapsto(0,z)$ [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison].

The maps $j_X:\Phi(X)\to\mathsf C(X)$, $(x,y)\mapsto(-y,x)$, with inverses $(y,x)\mapsto(x,-y)$, are natural chain isomorphisms. They induce a natural isomorphism of derived functors $Q\Phi(X)\xrightarrow{\rho_XQ(j_X)}R\lim X$. If $P$ is a complex and $\gamma_n:P\to X_n$ are strictly compatible chain maps, $u_\gamma=(\gamma_n)_n$, $\zeta_\gamma=(u_\gamma,0):P\to\Phi(X)$ and $\eta_\gamma=(0,u_\gamma):P\to\mathsf C(X)$, then
$$j_X\zeta_\gamma=\eta_\gamma,\qquad \rho_XQ(j_X)Q(\zeta_\gamma)=\operatorname{aug}_\gamma,$$
where $\operatorname{aug}_\gamma$ is the canonical derived strict augmentation $QP\to R\lim X$.

For any category $\mathcal H$, class $\mathcal W$ of its morphisms and localization $L:\mathcal H\to\mathcal D$ (the universal functor inverting $\mathcal W$), let $P$ and $X$ vary functorially on $\mathcal H$, with the $\gamma_n$ natural; assume $P(w)$ is a quasi-isomorphism and $X(w)$ a levelwise quasi-isomorphism for $w\in\mathcal W$. Then the displayed functors, units, isomorphisms and both equations descend uniquely through $L$, relative to the chosen functor factorizations. In particular their descended values do not depend on a representative or on the K-injective resolution.

proof.text:
The cone coordinates and diagonal maps are those of [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Since $f_X$ is a chain map, $d_\Phi^2(x,y)=(0,f_Xdx-df_Xx)=0$. Directly,
$$d_{\mathsf C}j_X(x,y)=(dy-f_Xx,dx)=j_Xd_\Phi(x,y).$$
The stated inverse has both composites equal to the identity. For a strict tower map $a:X\to Y$, its product map $b$ satisfies $bf_X=f_Yb$, and both $\mathsf C(a)j_X$ and $j_Y\Phi(a)$ send $(x,y)$ to $(-by,bx)$. Thus $j$ is a natural chain isomorphism.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison], $Q\mathsf C$ factors through $D(\operatorname{Tow}(\mathcal A))$ and has the specified natural isomorphism $\rho$ to $R\lim$. Naturality of $j$ gives $Q\Phi(a)=Q(j_Y)^{-1}Q\mathsf C(a)Q(j_X)$; hence $Q\Phi$ inverts quasi-isomorphisms. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] to the derived localization of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]: $Q\Phi$ and $Qj$ descend, and composing with $\rho$ gives the asserted natural derived isomorphism.

proof.text: Strict compatibility gives $\operatorname{pr}_nf_Xu_\gamma=\gamma_n-t_n\gamma_{n+1}=0$, so $f_Xu_\gamma=0$. Since $u_\gamma$ commutes with differentials, both $\zeta_\gamma$ and $\eta_\gamma$ are chain maps, and $j_X\zeta_\gamma=(0,u_\gamma)=\eta_\gamma$. This is precisely the strict augmentation constructed in [def-weil-strict-roos-model]. Its naturality follows by applying the product projections to the assumed naturality of each $\gamma_n$.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof; explicit signed-coordinate refinement written by Q25

proof.text: The last paragraph of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] says $\rho_XQ(\eta_\gamma)=\operatorname{aug}_\gamma$. Substituting step 3 proves the second equation. More explicitly, for its resolution $q:X\to I$, let $h:P\to\lim I$ have projections $q_n\gamma_n$ and let $\iota_I(z)=(0,z)$. Then $\mathsf C(q)\eta_\gamma=\iota_Ih$, so the stated normalization gives $\rho_XQ(\eta_\gamma)=Q(\iota_I)^{-1}Q(\iota_I)Qh=Qh$. The cited comparison asserts that this is the canonical augmentation independently of $q$.

proof.text: For the final localization, kernels and cokernels in [lem-weil-tower-category-levelwise-abelian] are levelwise, so cohomology is levelwise and $X(w)$ is a quasi-isomorphism of tower complexes. Thus $QP$, $QX$, $Q\mathsf C X$, $Q\Phi X$ and $R\lim QX$ invert $\mathcal W$. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property], relative to chosen factorizations all the natural maps of steps 1--4 descend uniquely; inverses, compositions and identities descend as well. Faithfulness there preserves both equations. Consequently representatives yield the same descended data under the factorization identifications; resolution independence was already supplied in step 4.
